subcategory: Vast 41-Sq-Km Reservoir with 48 Emerald Green Islets on Gomati River
description: Shaped like the small drum (Dambur) of Lord Shiva, an expansive 41-square-kilometer natural freshwater reservoir surrounded by rolling green hills, dotted with 48 emerald islets and the eco-island resort of Narkel Kunja (Coconut Island).
why_visit: Cruise on motorboats between 48 lush green islands, stay in luxury log huts at Narkel Kunja island, spot migratory winter waterfowl, and attend the colorful Tirthamukh Mela at the holy river confluence.
hidden_gem_reason: A tranquil 41-sq-km freshwater lake dotted with 48 green islands in rural Tripura, offering an offbeat island eco-stay away from commercial tourism.
best_time_to_visit: October to March (Winter migratory birds & pleasant boating weather)
activities: Island-Hopping Motorboat Cruise; Narkel Kunja Log Hut Stay; Winter Birdwatching; Water Sports; Tirthamukh Confluence Visit
notes: Equipped with high-speed water scooters and luxury floating cottages.

place_name: Unakoti Rock Carvings (Lost Hill of Faces)
subcategory: Ancient 7th-9th Century Rock-Cut Shaivite Colossal Bas-Reliefs
description: Dating back to the 7th-9th centuries, an extraordinary open-air pilgrimage site featuring colossal rock-cut bas-reliefs carved directly into forest hill slopes, centered around the 30-foot head of Shiva (Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava) with an ornate 10-foot headdress.
why_visit: Behold millions of ancient rock-cut stone faces emerging mysteriously from lush jungle cliffs and mountain streams, marvel at the 30-foot Shiva head, and attend the Ashokastami Mela in April.
hidden_gem_reason: An ancient open-air Shaivite wonderland hidden in dense rainforest hills, one of the most enigmatic archaeological wonders of Northeast India.
activities: Rock-Cut Bas-Relief Exploration; Archaeological Photography; Forest Stream Hiking; Ashokastami Pilgrimage
distance_from_nearest_famous_place: 20 km from Kailashahar / 175 km from Agartala
notes: Name 'Unakoti' means 'one less than a crore' (9,999,999) based on ancient Hindu folklore; tentative UNESCO World Heritage site.
